overview: The MPU9250 is what the MPU6050 would be with a compass added: the same 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope, plus a built-in 3-axis magnetometer (an AK8963 die inside the same package), giving nine degrees of freedom total. That magnetometer is the whole point — an accelerometer+gyroscope alone can tell you how a device is tilted, but not which way it's actually facing (north), because gyroscope-only heading drifts over time with no way to correct itself. Adding a magnetic compass reference is what makes a stable, drift-free heading possible, at the cost of needing to keep the sensor away from motors, speakers, and other magnetic interference sources.
simpleSummary: Like the MPU6050 but with a built-in compass added, for full 9-axis orientation sensing.

specifications.interface: I2C (default address 0x68), SPI on some breakouts

pinMap.name: AD0
pinMap.function: I2C address select — LOW sets address 0x68, HIGH sets 0x69.

pinMap.name: NCS
pinMap.function: SPI chip-select, on breakouts that expose an SPI mode — tie HIGH to stay in I2C mode.

pinMap.name: INT
pinMap.function: Interrupt output, configurable for new-data or motion events.

pinMap.name: FSYNC
pinMap.function: Frame sync input, used in advanced setups to align sampling with an external system.
pinMap.gotcha: Rarely used in hobbyist projects — safe to leave unconnected.

useCases.title: Drone/flight controller with stable heading
useCases.scenario: The magnetometer provides a drift-free compass heading that pure gyroscope integration can't.

useCases.title: AR/VR head or hand tracking
useCases.scenario: 9-DOF fusion for stable absolute orientation tracking.

useCases.title: Robot heading/compass navigation
useCases.scenario: Give a ground robot a stable sense of which way it's facing, independent of wheel-slip-based dead reckoning.

oftenConfusedWith: BNO055 (does sensor fusion onboard instead of raw data)
oftenUpgradedTo: BNO055 for onboard sensor fusion instead of writing your own filter
